solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/power-of-four/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

342. Power of Four

Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of four. Otherwise, return false.

An integer n is a power of four, if there exists an integer x such that n == 4^x.

Example 1:

Input: n = 16
Output: true

Example 2:

Input: n = 5
Output: false

Example 3:

Input: n = 1
Output: true

Constraints:

    -2^31 <= n <= 2^31 - 1

Follow up: Could you solve it without loops/recursion?
"""


class Solution:
    def isPowerOfFour(self, n: int) -> bool:
        # A number n is a power of four if:
        # 1) n > 0
        # 2) n is a power of two (only one bit set)
        # 3) the only set bit is in an even position (0-indexed from right)
        # For example, 4^0=1 (bit 0), 4^1=4 (bit 2), 4^2=16 (bit 4), etc.
        if n <= 0:
            return False
        # Check if n is power of two: n & (n-1) == 0
        if n & (n - 1) != 0:
            return False
        # Check if the single set bit is in the correct position for power of four
        # 0x55555555 is a mask with bits set at all odd positions (1-based), i.e. even positions 0-based
        return (n & 0x55555555) != 0


sol = Solution()

print(sol.isPowerOfFour(16))  # True

assert sol.isPowerOfFour(16) is True
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(5) is False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(1) is True

assert sol.isPowerOfFour(0) == False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(-4) == False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(2) == False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(64) == True
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(1024) == True
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(1073741824) == True
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(2147483647) == False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(-2147483648) == False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(3) == False
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(256) == True
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(4) == True
assert sol.isPowerOfFour(8) == False
